expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Amended, no new file: tickets.md gains TKT-014..TKT-017 (lines 134-187) and cli.md gains CLI-010..CLI-012 (lines 78-130); CLI-001 and CLI-006 are edited in place. Why, transcript.md:154: 'Decision: amend, not create. The overdue rule is a ticket rule and belongs with TKT-005. The `list` line is CLI-006 and the command set is CLI-001. A new file would restate or contradict those.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro, one paragraph at tickets.md:96-99: 'Support agents see which tickets missed their due time, and can list only those tickets. The list of overdue tickets starts with the ticket that has been overdue longest...' (a Status paragraph and a paragraph on the TODOs follow). 'Prefix: `TKT`.' at tickets.md:16, 'Prefix: `CLI`.' at cli.md:8. 'Non-goals.' at tickets.md:120 with 8 boundaries, e.g. 'No alerts. An agent learns that a ticket is overdue only from `list` or `overdue`.' (128) and 'No change to due times. The hours of TKT-005 stay. There are no business hours, no paused clock, and no due time set by hand.' (126).

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 7 new criteria headed '### PREFIX-NNN: Title': TKT-014..TKT-017 and CLI-010..CLI-012; CLI-001 and CLI-006 edited. check_run: duplicates 0 and testable_lines 0 in both files. Body length, noted not failed: by a rough sentence count 6 of 7 new bodies run past three sentences (CLI-011 about 16 sentences and 171 words in five paragraphs, TKT-014 11, TKT-016 9, TKT-017 8 with a table, CLI-010 8 with a table, TKT-015 6, TODO paragraphs included); mean about 113 words.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: cli.md:80-82 (CLI-010) '`ticketdesk list` prints the word `OVERDUE` on the line of each ticket that is overdue per TKT-014. The word sits between the priority and the state.' Filter and order: cli.md:109-111 (CLI-011) 'prints one line per overdue ticket, in the order of TKT-017... It prints no other ticket' and tickets.md:173-175 (TKT-017) 'It sorts them by due time ascending, so the ticket that has been overdue longest comes first.' Exact due time: tickets.md:137-138 (TKT-014) 'At the exact due time the ticket is not overdue yet.' Closed: tickets.md:153 (TKT-015) 'A `closed` ticket is not overdue, whenever it was closed.' Nothing overdue: cli.md:116 (CLI-011) 'With no overdue ticket, `overdue` prints nothing and exits with code 0.'

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: check_run impl_words=0 in both files; no .py name, function, class, or module in any new or edited body. Outcomes are output lines and exit codes, e.g. CLI-012 'prints usage to stderr and exits with code 2. It prints nothing to stdout.' Borderline, not failed: TKT-014 says 'The current time is the time on the machine's clock when the command runs. It is in seconds since the Unix epoch, like the `at` of an event, see LOG-004', a representation detail the user cannot see; it names no code. The CLI-001 TODO links to the sibling spec file `tickets.md`, a doc cross-reference.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: tickets.md:11-14: 'Overdue is worked out from the due time and the current time each time a command runs. The proposal assumes that it is never a state and never an event'. tickets.md:161-163 (TKT-016): 'A ticket that becomes overdue keeps its state, its assignee, and its due time. No event is appended when the due time passes, so the log file stays byte for byte the same.' The alternative is flagged with the specs it would change, tickets.md:166-169: 'A state that an event records also changes LOG-002 and LOG-003. A state that the time decides also changes INV-001 and LOG-009. Confirm with the user.' INV-002 is not cited by ID; the behavior respects it.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-005 reused: tickets.md:137 (TKT-014) 'The due time is the one of TKT-005.' and the non-goal at 126. List order kept: cli.md:88-89 (CLI-010) 'The order of the lines does not change, see TKT-013.' and cli.md:45 (CLI-006) still reads 'in ID order, see TKT-013'. The due-time order applies only to the overdue listing (TKT-017).

expectations.text: docs/product-specs/README.md is updated: the new file appears in the prefix table and the index with a one-line summary (or, if criteria were appended to an existing file, the README needed no change and the spec says so).
expectations.evidence: Criteria were appended to existing files, so the prefix table needs no new row and is unchanged. The index row for tickets.md was updated, README.md:80: '...due time by priority, listing. Overdue tickets: goals, non-goals, the overdue rule, the overdue listing order.' The cli.md row is unchanged and still accurate. AGENTS.md got the matching row and a 'Specified, not built' line.

expectations.text: Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.
expectations.evidence: No end list in the spec; questions.md lists 10 questions with the assumption and criterion ID for each, which the assertion allows. Inline marks sit under the criteria as TODO paragraphs: tickets.md:148 'TODO: the request says tickets that "pass their due time". This text reads that as strictly later than the due time. Confirm with the user.'; 156 (closed late); 166 (marker, not a fourth state); 186 (tie order); cli.md:98 (marker position, with a three-option table); cli.md:122 (no due time shown, exit code 0). tickets.md:105 says 'The `TODO:` paragraphs under TKT-014 to TKT-017, CLI-010, and CLI-011 are open questions.' Only questions.md Q8 (lines of other tickets stay unchanged) has no mark in the spec; it is a no-change constraint stated as goal 3, which the other runs state without a question. Nothing is resolved silently. Bar used for all six runs: an assumption counts as marked when the spec itself flags it and ties it to the criterion, by a mark under the criterion or by an in-spec list entry that names the criterion ID.

expectations.text: Skim test: the intro paragraph's first sentence says what the feature is for a support agent; each criterion title names the behavior; no lead is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: One paragraph lead is a teaser. cli.md:122, inside CLI-011: 'TODO: two assumptions need the user.' It announces a count of unnamed things, the form assets/writing.md gives as a teaser ('Two things went wrong.'). prose-lint misses it only because of the 'TODO:' prefix: on a scratch copy with the prefix stripped it reports 'cli.md:122: teaser-lead: Lead announces a count of things without naming them.' The same stripped-prefix sweep reports 0 findings for the other five runs, so the bar is the same in both arms. The rest of the skim test holds: intro first sentence, tickets.md:96, 'Support agents see which tickets missed their due time, and can list only those tickets.'; titles name behaviors ('A closed ticket is never overdue', 'Overdue changes nothing else', 'OVERDUE marker in list', 'overdue takes no arguments'), with 'CLI-011: overdue' a bare command name in the repo's style. Also noted: the new file-header paragraph at tickets.md:11 leads with a definition, 'An `open` or `assigned` ticket whose due time has passed is overdue.'; it is not the feature intro.
